title: Fitted V-Neck Top Sewing Pattern – Free PDF
content:
Garment Fitted woven top with a deep V neckline and short sleeves

Level Confident beginner

Sizes US 00 – 22 (XXS – 4XL)

Fabric Linen, linen-viscose, cotton poplin, viscose crepe or chambray

Pieces 5

This free v neck top sewing pattern gives you a close-fitting woven blouse with a deep V neckline, short set-in sleeves and a gently curved hem. Bust darts at the front and long darts at the back shape it to the body, and an invisible zipper hidden in the side seam lets it slip on without any buttons.

→ Jump to the free download

1 cm (3/8″) seam allowance included on all pieces · 2 cm (3/4″) hem on the blouse and sleeves · invisible zipper 40–45 cm (16–18″)

Design details of the fitted v neck top

It is a classic dressmaker blouse with a clean, modern line. A short bust dart on each side of the front, a shoulder dart and a long double-pointed waist dart on each back panel and a centre back seam give the close shape, with about 5.5 cm of ease at the bust. The V neckline is finished with an interfaced facing, so there is no binding and no topstitching around the neck.

Reading the sketch

On the front, the two straight lines that meet in a point are the V neckline; the short line inside it is the back neckline you see through the V. The short horizontal lines at the sides are the bust darts. There is no seam down the middle and no button or zipper on the front.

On the back, the long line in the middle is the centre back seam. The two short lines near the neck are shoulder darts and the two long lines lower down are waist darts, pointed at both ends. The zipper is invisible, in the left side seam.

  • Deep V neckline with the point at mid-chest, finished with an interfaced facing
  • Short fitted set-in sleeves with a 2 cm (3/4″) hem
  • Side bust darts at the front, shoulder darts and double-pointed waist darts at the back
  • Centre back seam and an invisible zipper in the left side seam, opening from the hem
  • Hip length with a gently curved front hem

It is a lovely next step after your first easy tops: you will practise darts, a V-neck facing with a sharp point, an invisible zipper and set-in sleeves, and end up with a blouse that fits like a made-to-measure one.

Sizing guide

Measure your bust around the fullest part and pick the size from the table, then check your waist and hips. This top is close fitting: between two sizes, choose by the bust and blend the waist at the side seams. Not sure how to measure? See how to take body measurements and how to choose your sewing pattern size.

US sizes 00 to 22, drafted for a height of 167.75 cm (5 ft 6 in). Letter sizes are a guide only: 00 = XXS · 0–2 = XS · 4–6 = S · 8–10 = M · 12–14 = L · 16 = XL · 18 = 2XL · 20 = 3XL · 22 = 4XL. Always choose by measurements.

Body measurements

Finished top measurements

There is about 5.5 cm (2 1/8″) of ease at the bust and 10 cm (4″) at the waist. Back length is measured at the centre back from the neckline to the finished hem; front length from the shoulder at the neck straight down to the hem.

Fabric amounts

Estimated with every piece laid out for each size, plus about 8 % for shrinkage and straightening. Buy a little more for a one-way print, stripes or checks, and pre-wash the fabric before cutting. A longer zipper is fine: it is shortened at the top.

Common fit adjustments

Length. The top is drafted for 167.75 cm and ends at the hip. Change the front and back by the same amount between the waist notch and the hip, so the darts keep their place. Full guide: how to lengthen or shorten a sewing pattern.

Neckline depth. The point of the V sits about 15 cm (6″) below the base of the neck in size 8. To raise it, trace the front and the front neck facing and move the point up by the same amount on both, keeping the lines straight.

Materials

  • Main fabric: 1.0 to 1.8 m (1 1/8 to 2 yd) of a light to medium-weight woven with a soft drape
  • Interfacing: 0.3 m (3/8 yd) of light fusible interfacing for the neck facings
  • Zipper: one invisible zipper, 45 cm (18″) for sizes 00–8, 40 cm (16″) for sizes 10–22
  • Thread: polyester all-purpose thread
  • Tools: invisible zipper foot, universal needle 70 to 80, a tailor's ham for pressing the darts
  • Pins or clips, chalk or a washable marker

Pattern pieces

  • 1 Front: cut 1 on a single layer, right side up (drawn whole)
  • 2 Back: cut 2, a left and a right piece
  • 3 Sleeve: cut 2, a left and a right sleeve
  • 4 Front neck facing: cut 1 + 1 in interfacing (drawn whole)
  • 5 Back neck facing: cut 2 + 2 in interfacing

Choosing fabric for a v neck top

A fitted top with darts likes a woven that drapes softly but still holds a crisp line at the V. Linen and linen-viscose blends give the easy summer look you see in our photos; cotton poplin, cotton lawn and chambray are perfect for everyday versions, and a viscose crepe or challis turns it into a polished office blouse.

Because the top is close fitting, a woven with 2 to 3 % elastane is comfortable without changing the size. Avoid knits and very slippery fabrics such as satin or chiffon: the V point and the invisible zipper will be hard to keep neat. More tips in how to choose fabric for sewing patterns.

New to PDF patterns? Start here

Our free step-by-step guides take you from your measurements to a printed pattern:

  1. How to take your body measurements: what to measure and how, in 10 minutes.
  2. How to choose your size: which measurement to follow, and what to do between sizes.
  3. How to print and assemble your pattern: A4 or US Letter, the test box, and taping the pages. Then learn how to read a sewing pattern: symbols and markings explained.

Sewing notes

Fit and style

A close fit from bust to hip. Pin the darts and the side seams and try the top on before you set the zipper if you are between sizes.

Fabric

Wovens only. Press every dart over a tailor's ham and use a pressing cloth on linen and viscose to avoid shine.

Zipper

The invisible zipper opens from the hem. See how to sew a zipper.

Get the pattern

Free PDF pattern, one file per size, US sizes 00 to 22 (XXS to 4XL). Share your make with #sewcraftly!

Download A4
Download US Letter

Print page 1 at 100% and check that the test square measures 10 cm (4 in). New to PDF patterns? Read how to print and assemble a PDF pattern.

Sewing steps

Seam allowance 1 cm (3/8″) unless stated otherwise. Sew right sides together and press every seam and dart before it is crossed by another one.

  1. Prepare. Fuse interfacing to the front and back neck facings. Transfer the darts, notches and the ZIP notches of the left side seam. Staystitch the front and back necklines 8 mm from the edge, pivoting at the V point with the needle down.
  2. Front darts. Sew the bust darts from the side seam towards the point, knot the thread tails at the point and press the darts down.
  3. Back darts. Sew the shoulder darts from the shoulder towards the point. Sew the waist darts from point to point through the widest part, knot the threads, clip the fold at the widest part and press all back darts towards the centre.
  4. Centre back seam. Sew the two backs together from the neckline to the hem, matching the waist notches. Finish and press open.
  5. Shoulders. Pin the front to the back at the shoulders, stitch, finish the edges separately and press the seams open.
  6. Neck facing. Join the front neck facing to the two back neck facings at the shoulders and at the centre back, and finish the outer edge. Sew the facing to the neckline, shortening the stitch near the V and pivoting exactly at the point. Trim, clip into the V and the curves, understitch, turn the facing inside and tack it at the shoulders.
  7. Side seams. Sew the right side seam from the armhole to the hem. On the left side, stitch only from the armhole to the upper ZIP notch, about 2.5 cm below the underarm. Finish both sides and press open.
  8. Invisible zipper. Place the zipper upside down in the open part of the left side seam, top stops just below the hemline, and stitch each tape from the hem up to the upper ZIP notch with an invisible zipper foot. Shorten the zipper above the notch if needed.
  9. Sleeves. Easestitch the sleeve cap between the circles, sew the underarm seam and hem the sleeve 2 cm (3/4″). Set the sleeve into the armhole, matching the top notch to the shoulder seam, ease the cap and stitch. Stitch again 6 mm from the edge and finish.
  10. Hem. Finish the lower edge, turn up 2 cm (3/4″) and stitch, folding the hem allowance over the zipper tape so the hem edges sit next to the coil. Give the top a final press.

Printable sewing tutorial

Need help completing the project?

Get the full printable tutorial for the Fitted V-Neck Top: detailed step-by-step sewing instructions with clear illustrations, a sizing guide, fabric amounts per size and the list of materials you need.

  • Illustrated diagrams for every step, from the darts and the V-neck facing to the invisible zipper and the sleeves
  • Size charts in cm and inches, finished measurements and fabric amounts per size
  • Video guides for the key techniques, with links and QR codes
  • Printable PDF with A0 pattern files, instant download
Shop now

Tips and common mistakes

A V point that puckers. Shorten the stitch for 2 cm on each side of the point, stop with the needle down exactly on it before you pivot, and clip into the point right up to the stitching. Understitch as far into the V as you can.

Dart tips that bubble. Sew the last 2 cm of each dart right along the fold, do not backstitch at the tip, knot the threads instead and press over a tailor's ham.

A zipper that shows. Press the coil flat from the wrong side before you start and stitch as close to the teeth as the invisible zipper foot allows, from the hem up to the notch.

A sleeve cap with tucks. Pull the ease threads only between the circles, spread the fullness evenly and sew with the sleeve on the bottom so the feed dogs help ease it in.

How to style a v neck top

Everyday: untucked over high-waisted cream or white trousers and flat sandals, as in our photos.

Office: in viscose crepe, tucked into a pencil or midi skirt. It pairs beautifully with our free wide leg pants sewing pattern.

Weekend: in a small floral lawn with light-wash jeans, or in linen with our free flare pants sewing pattern for a matching summer outfit.

Care

Wash at 30 °C on a gentle cycle, inside out, with the zipper closed. Dry on a hanger and press from the wrong side; use a pressing cloth on linen and viscose and a little steam on the darts.

Questions

Is seam allowance included?

Yes: 1 cm (3/8″) on every seam, a 2 cm (3/4″) hem on the blouse and on the sleeves, and 7 mm (1/4″) on the outer edges of the neck facings, which are only finished.

Which paper sizes are included?

The free download has A4 and US Letter files, one file per size, so you only print the size you need.

Which size should I choose?

Choose by your bust measurement in the size chart, not by your shop size. The top is close fitting, with about 5.5 cm (2 1/8″) of ease at the bust: between two sizes, choose by the bust and blend the waist at the side seams.

How do I get it on?

An invisible zipper in the left side seam opens from the hem up to just below the underarm, so the fitted top slips on easily without a back opening.

Is this v neck top hard to sew?

It is a good confident-beginner project. There are five pieces, and you will practise darts, a V-neck facing with a sharp point, an invisible zipper and set-in sleeves.

What fabric works best?

A light to medium-weight woven with a soft drape: linen or a linen-viscose blend, cotton poplin or lawn, viscose crepe or challis, chambray or a light crepe. A woven with 2 to 3 % elastane adds comfort. Knits are not suitable.

Can I make it longer or shorter?

Yes. The pattern is drafted for a height of 167.75 cm (5 ft 6 in). Lengthen or shorten the front and back by the same amount between the waist notch and the hip; the lower zipper notch stays on the hemline, so choose the zipper length again.
